description.p: Hue is a straightforward raster paint application for the GNOME desktop, in the spirit of the classic Paint. It gives you the core drawing tools and gets out of the way.

ul.li: Pencil, brush and eraser
Line, rectangle and ellipse, filled or outlined, with Shift for squares, circles and 45° lines
Text in any font installed on the system
Flood fill and colour picker
Rectangular selection to move, copy, cut, stretch or crop to
Paste screenshots and drop images straight onto the canvas
Zoom from 10% to 800%, with crisp pixels when zoomed in
Rotate and flip the whole image, and resize the canvas by dragging its edge
Undo and redo history, and a list of recently opened files
Keyboard shortcuts you can change to suit you
A colour palette along the bottom, under the tools or beside the canvas

description.p: Hue works entirely offline: it never connects to the network and keeps every image on your own machine.

screenshot.caption: The main window with a blank canvas

ul.li: Change any keyboard shortcut from the new Keyboard Shortcuts window (Ctrl+?)
Place the colour palette along the bottom, under the tools or right of the canvas
The image is centred when the window has room around it, such as when maximised
Scroll over the zoom level in the bottom bar to zoom in or out
A refreshed look, with the canvas set in a rounded card inside one continuous frame
The window closes on the first click when there are no unsaved changes
Zoom with Ctrl+scroll or Ctrl+plus and minus, with crisp pixels when zoomed in
Rotate, flip and crop the image to a selection
Stretch a selection or a pasted image with its handles, and nudge it with the arrow keys
Shift draws squares, circles and 45° lines
Recent Files, and a quality setting when saving as JPEG
Saving can no longer destroy the original file if it fails
Images too large to edit are refused instead of exhausting memory
Flood fill is many times faster
Undo history is capped by memory, and undoing back to the saved image clears the unsaved-changes marker
The Flatpak no longer needs access to the Pictures folder
Fixed missing toolbar icons in the Flatpak

description.p: First release with the core drawing tools.
